text: Literature is one of the most powerful forms of cultural diplomacy, said Deputy Minister Viktor Stoyanov in Thessaloniki (06.05.2026 21:27)

Literature is one of the most powerful forms of cultural diplomacy, said Acting Deputy Minister of Culture Viktor Stoyanov during the opening of the International Book Fair in Thessaloniki, at which Bulgaria is the guest of honor.

"Literature builds trust, promotes understanding and creates lasting bonds between peoples. Our presence in Thessaloniki is not only a celebration of Bulgarian literature – it is a celebration of the lasting friendship between Bulgaria and Greece. We are not only closest neighbors and reliable allies in NATO and the EU – we are closest friends in spirit, and our peoples share deep respect and affection for each other," Deputy Minister Stoyanov noted in his speech.
He pointed out that it is a privilege for Bulgaria to be the focal country of this year's forum, and that this "embodies the spirit of dialogue and shared cultural horizons in our region."

"The literary ties between Bulgaria and Greece are deep, vibrant and enduring. For decades, our cultures have been engaged in dialogue through poetry, prose and translation. Greek poetry, with its philosophical depth and lyrical power, has left a lasting mark on Bulgarian literature. At the same time, Bulgarian authors have found a receptive and insightful audience in Greek readers," he added.

The Deputy Minister noted the merit of personalities from the past and present, among whom he listed the names of Stefan Gechev - diplomat, translator and writer, Georgi Koufov - translator of Nikos Kazantzakis, Kostas Varnalis and others. He also noted contemporary authors such as Yana Bukova, Georgi Gospodinov, Rene Karabash, Teodora Dimova and Elena Alexieva, who have been translated into Greek.

Viktor Stoyanov also drew attention to the important work of translators. "In the last three years alone, more than 200 Bulgarian titles have been translated into foreign languages, with over ten of them into Greek. These numbers reflect a clear and encouraging trend - Bulgarian literature is reaching an increasingly wider audience and building significant international connections," he believes.

The event was also attended by Nikolaos Bakunakis - Chairman of the Greek Foundation for Books and Culture, Christos Tsendemeidis - Chairman of the Thessaloniki International Exhibition and Congress Center (TIF-HELEXPO S.A.), Lina Mendoni - Minister of Culture of Greece, Konstantinos Gyulekas - Deputy Minister of Interior of Greece with responsibility for Thrace and Macedonia, Athina Aidona - Governor of the Central Macedonia Region, Stelios Angeloudis - Mayor of Thessaloniki, Anton Markov - Consul General of Bulgaria in Thessaloniki, Teodora Dimova - Bulgarian writer and others.
The official opening of the Bulgarian stand will be on Thursday. "Literature Beyond Borders" is the central theme of the Bulgarian participation.
